Strategy: Take the median-ranked bin. Prefer the bin whose residual ranks in the middle of all open bins, counting residuals below it, robust to a few very loose bins. This skips the tightest bins, kept for exact fits, and the loosest bins, kept for big items, so ranking can differ from Best Fit whenever the median bin is not the tightest. It may help by filling representative bins, but may fail by stranding tight bins if later items run large.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    n = len(bins)
    return [-abs(sum([1 for s in bins if s < r]) - (n - 1) / 2) for r in bins]
```
generator_note: Median-rank targeting: prefer bin whose residual rank is closest to (n-1)/2.
